title: Next multi-stream loop draft
first_prompt:
<pasted_content id="5e38">

Let's start working on draft for our next multi-agent stream, which will be a 4 parallel agent effort. Do this on a new branch so as not to disturb agents building new fe

commits.summary: run-verification skill: say how to wait for a background runner
commits.body: Step 2 told the managing agent to start 'pipeline.py run' in the background but not how to wait for it. A verification-loop session improvised 'while pgrep -f "pipeline.py run"; do sleep 10; done' and an 'until ! pgrep -f ...' loop; each matched its own command line, so the session hung for 8 minutes after the runner had finished, until it was killed by hand at 19:49. Step 2 now says to wait for the background task's completion notification or poll 'pipeline.py status' until it shows 'running: 0', and never to wait with pgrep -f on a pattern. A documentation change only; checked that 'status' prints a 'running:' line.

commits.summary: Record the own checker's solver calls as replayable incremental CNF transcripts (Phase 6a)
commits.body: A check by the own checker can now write every clause it gives CaDiCaL and every call it makes, in order, as CaDiCaL's incremental CNF (p inccnf), each call followed by a comment with its answer, its time and its per-call limit, under a header naming the tool, the solver, the method and the engine's options. The new lib/src/bmc/transcript.rs writes and replays them. bmc::Options::transcript names a file; otherwise JVMCONTRACT_TRANSCRIPTS names a directory and each check writes PID-N.icnf there, which reaches prove, equivalence and the benchmark's runner without a flag. jvmcontract transcript FILE runs one again on the bundled CaDiCaL with the recorded limits and reports times and contradicting answers (exit 1). Phase 6c judges solvers on these sequences, since a check is hundreds of incremental calls with model-dependent lemmas between them.

commits.summary: Put the own checker's SAT solver behind a narrow interface (Phase 6b)
commits.body:
The own checker's solver is now reached only through a Sat trait (lib/src/bmc/sat.rs: signature, add_clause, set_limit, solve under assumptions, value, variables), with CaDiCaL 1.9.5 as the bundled crate gives it as its one implementation. That separates the engine's three layers: scheduling the queries (Engine in bmc/mod.rs: probes, deferred paths, the refinement loop), encoding them (Blaster in bmc/bits.rs, which now holds a Box<dyn Sat> and calls nothing else of the solver), and solving them. bmc::Options::solver chooses the solver a check runs on (CaDiCaL by default), and transcript::replay_on replays a transcript on any solver behind the trait, so Phase 6c can put Bitwuzla's SAT mode behind it without touching the engine. The transcript's header now names the solver the check ran on. Results still name CaDiCaL through solver_signature(), since nothing outside tests sets another solver.

No behaviour changes. A new engine test runs a check on a test double that logs everything crossing the trait: it gives the plain run's outcome, its clauses and calls match the outcome's counts and the transcript's, and a replay on the logged solver gives the same clauses and calls again. End to end, held/lower-bound (equivalence --engine native, unwind 9, arrays up to 8) writes the same transcripts by count as before the change: 460 calls over 43,478 clauses and 13,025 variables, verified, plus a 5-call check, both replaying with no contradiction. Unit (153), integration (64) and skill tests pass. Conformance fails only its two known tests: 12 library-record claims (JDK 25.0.5 against a record made on 25.0.4.1) and the JBMC stream's benchmark file. The brief's Progress records this, the shared file changed (lib/README.md), and the next step: enums in the own checker.

commits.summary: JBMC right-shifts by the whole distance: the preflight names an unmasked shift and refuses a JBMC proof through one
commits.body:
Found while reading step 2b's benchmark job 20261106-201041 (passed) for 2c: the one case whose class differed between JBMC's staging policies, conformance/shiftRight/2, has a counterexample under full-range and tight (x = -2147483648, s = 33) that does not reproduce. JBMC 6.11.0 masks the distance of the left shifts (--show-goto-functions: shl(x, bitand(s, 31))) but not of the right ones (ashr(x, s), lshr), for int and long, so a distance outside 0..31 (0..63) fills the value with its sign or zeros where the JVM shifts by the distance's low bits. It also gave false proofs under strict: x >> s where s == 33, asserting result == 0 || result == -1, was verified by JBMC under both policies, while the JVM gives shiftRight(4, 33) == 2; likewise x >>> s == 0 where s == 32. The own checker refutes both.

lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs gains a third Defect, unmasked-shift: a right shift whose distance is not a constant within the width, nor its bitwise and with one, computed by instructions no branch joins. As with step 3's two, a JBMC proof that reaches one is refused under every --gaps mode and a counterexample is still replayed, its message naming the defect. The rule is broad (conformance/shiftRight/1, a correct JBMC proof under x == -1, is now refused; auto proves it on the own checker); constant distances are untouched. In the apps only Quorum's Backoff has a variable right shift, and its JBMC examples (016, 019) are violations.

Verified: the preflight's fixture test (renamed the_preflight_names_where_jbmc_runs_the_bytecode_otherwise_than_the_jvm) covers 3 new defects and 3 neighbours (s & 31, >> 1, <<) and fails with the detection disabled. The corpus gains conformance/shiftRight/3 and shiftUnsigned/3, the two false proofs, which agree with the JVM on the own checker; lib/benchmark/conformance.json is regenerated (98 claims). On the real JBMC both are now refused naming the defect, and auto gives the violation. Lib 157, integration 63, skill, test_run.py and test_gap_table.py pass; conformance fails only on its 12 known JDK 25.0.5 disagreements. A draft upstream report for this cause is in lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/README.md, its reproducer checked on JBMC and the JVM; not filed.

Shared files changed, added to: lib/tests/conformance.rs (two claims and a call), lib/README.md (a sentence). Progress also records the three collected jobs: -201041 passed (2c next); -203452 failed in its integration step (a JBMC timeout on Pricing#total) and under auto --confirm; -204220 (4a) failed because the examples' result schema does not allow 1b's stated.checker.sat, to fix and resubmit.

commits.summary: JBMC searches the full range alone by default, on benchmark job 20261106-201041's evidence
commits.body:
Step 2c of engine-priorities.md. Job 20261106-201041 ran the corpus under JBMC's three staging policies. Under strict, JBMC's proofs were the same 54 of 65 under each, in 654 s under staged, 575 s under full-range and 588 s under tight; the hard ones took half the time without the stages (bounded binary search 26 s against 56 s, example 141 31 s against 61 s). Counterexamples took 9 s against 27 s, no shrunk witness was larger, and no run under full-range was starved. Under auto the policies gave the same verdicts. The one case whose class changed, conformance/shiftRight/2, is JBMC's unmasked right shift (the previous commit), which staged's witness happened to miss; it is not a worse verdict of the policy, and is now the one case where --engine jbmc answers unverifiable where it gave a violation (the own checker and auto decide it).

So full-range is now the default of --jbmc-staging on prove and equivalence, of Options::new in property.rs and equivalence.rs, and of lib/benchmark/run.py. deadline.rs's module comment records the evidence. The own checker keeps its stages, as decided, and --confirm already ran the full range. lib/README.md and lib/benchmark/README.md describe the new default with the job's figures.

commits.summary: Under --confirm, a JBMC refutation through a named defect, whose witness does not reproduce, is no verdict; job 20261106-203452 triaged (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-203452 (step 3 of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md) failed two of its three steps. Its --confirm step had 12 disagreements, all on conformance/caught, caughtAsRuntime and nestedHandler under strict and assume: the own checker proves the claim, and JBMC's confirming run refutes it at n = 0 through return-past-handler or stubbed-handler, the defects step 3 found and guards against, on a witness the interpreter does not reproduce. The tool called that a disagreement. Now equivalence::confirm runs JBMC's preflight on a refutation too, and takes the caller's replay of the witness in the harness: when the preflight names a defect and the witness does not reproduce, the refutation is the defect's, as a JBMC proof through one is refused, so the confirmation is no-verdict and the own checker's proof stands, unconfirmed, the line naming the defects. A witness that reproduces is still a disagreement, as is one with no defect in reach.

Its integration step failed at the own checker's regression proof of fixtures.Pricing#total in the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs, not at JBMC as the brief's Progress had said. Inline on cvm, 2 of 8 identical runs ran out of 40 s where the others took 4 s: the own checker's branch probes are budgeted by wall-clock time, so its path order depends on timing. That is lib/src/bmc/, the native stream's, so it is recorded under Progress with a reproducer for the native stream and the reconcile loop, and nothing there changed. That step's tee also failed, since lib/target did not exist yet in the job's fresh checkout.

Verified: on the real JBMC (milliseconds), caught, caughtAsRuntime and nestedHandler under auto --confirm are now verified, not confirmed, naming the defect. A new test, confirm_takes_a_refutation_through_a_jbmc_defect_for_no_verdict, uses a stand-in JBMC whose program reaches caught, for prove and equivalence, and fails with the fix disabled. Lib 157 tests and the conformance tests pass, except the corpus's 12 known disagreements from the contract records (JDK 25.0.5 against 25.0.4.1). lib/README.md's --confirm paragraph says so. Shared files changed: lib/tests/conformance.rs (fake_jbmc reads an optional goto.txt; the test), equivalence.rs and property.rs (confirm's closure and its two calls), lib/README.md.

Job 20261106-231317 reruns the three steps, with lib/target created first. The corpus under JBMC and auto also hasn't run since the unmasked-shift claims and the full-range default went in.

commits.summary: The examples' result schema allows the statement's SAT solver record; 4a's job rerun (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-204220, step 4a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md (the 41 recorded JBMC examples under strict on both engines), stopped in both engine steps at its first example: build.py refused 013's result against examples/schema/result.schema.json because 'sat' was unexpected. Verified inline: real sat records from a millisecond proof on each engine, spliced into the 14 committed results that carry a statement, pass build.py's whole validation (flat schema, round trip through the stored format, stored schema), and a record with an extra field is refused; three real statements (own checker, JBMC, auto --confirm) validate in full against $defs/statement; test_build.py has the same 35 pre-existing errors before and after the change, and test_gap_table.py passes.

Job 20261106-231837 reruns -204220's three steps unchanged at this commit, so it also measures the unmasked-shift guard, --confirm's rule for refutations through a defect, and the full-range default on the examples. The stream's status is now waiting on jobs 20261106-231317 and 20261106-231837.

commits.summary: The examples' result schema allows a run's phasesExcess; 3's rerun passed, 4a's JBMC table measured, its own-checker step rerun (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-231317, the rerun of step 3's job (llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md), passed: 63 integration tests, the corpus under jbmc and auto (98 claims, 196 runs, the unmasked-shift claims and the full-range default included) and under auto --confirm, where the 12 disagreements of -203452 are gone. Phase 3 is done: the cause of the witnesses that don't reproduce is known, guarded with tests, and drafted as reports for the user.

Job 20261106-231837, step 4a's rerun, measured JBMC's per-obligation table under strict over the 41 recorded JBMC examples: 43 obligations, 27 refuted, 13 established, 3 unresolved. 071#0 and #1 are no verdict at the Enum.<init>, List.of and List.copyOf stubs, as job -082917 projected. 037#0, the one example that differs from its expected verdict, is a JBMC proof refused by the unmasked-shift guard at -1 >>> Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(cap - 1), whose distance is 32 when cap == 1. Each run in examples/schema/result.schema.json may now carry phasesExcess, a positive number. Job 20261107-000039 reruns -231837's three steps unchanged at this commit, so the own checker's table and the comparison come from one commit. The stream's status is now waiting on it.

commits.summary: 4a's job 20261107-000039 passed: both engines' strict tables over the 41 JBMC examples, and their comparison; the stream's phases are done
commits.body: Job 20261107-000039, step 4a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md, passed (4 m 22 s, peak 1.1 GiB). It ran build.py on the 41 recorded B9/B11 JBMC examples under --gaps strict on each engine, in scratch copies, and saved gap_table.py --json for each. JBMC's table is row for row the one job -231837 measured: of 43 obligations, 27 refuted, 13 established, 3 unresolved (071#0 and #1 at the Enum.<init>, List.of and List.copyOf stubs; 037#0 a correct proof refused by the unmasked-shift guard). The own checker's: 24 refuted, 11 established, 8 unresolved, at Quorum's TermOrder.<clinit> (013#0, 071#0-#2), at Integer/Long.numberOfLeadingZeros, which strict refuses (037#0, 127#0), at a float parameter (035#0) and at --unwind 16 (052#0). The engines agree on all 35 obligations both decide; JBMC alone decides 5 (013#0, 035#0, 052#0, 071#2, 127#0), the own checker alone none, and neither 3. commits.summary: Record session traces
commits.body: The engines-jbmc stream's last turns, recorded by the reconcile loop of engine-priorities.md before the merge, so its conversation follows its last commit on its branch. No code changed.

commits.summary: Run enums in the own checker: arrays of references, Enum's model, switch maps (Phase 5, step 3)
commits.body:
The own checker (lib/src/bmc) now has arrays of references: anewarray, aaload and aastore, a cell holding an object or null. An index that is an input splits the path per cell, since a reference is not a choice among bits, and a path that runs the instruction again at a join does so without waiting there, so that merging does not make its constant a choice again. An array's clone() is a copy, an aastore that would throw ArrayStoreException is refused, and arrays are named by descriptor, as ClassPath::is_subtype names them. The model of java.lang.Enum in lib/models, until now on JBMC's class path only, is run by the own checker too (models::CHECKER_RUNS, ClassPath::checker_model, checker_method, checker_runs); the interpreter keeps its natives and JBMC's class path is unchanged. Enum initializers, $VALUES and javac's $SwitchMap classes therefore run where the JVM runs them. The gap scan agrees: anewarray is no longer refused, an array clone is exact, and an abstract application method is no longer counted as a JDK gap (an earlier flaw that an enum with constant bodies showed under --gaps advised).

Checked: five new conformance cases (enumValues, enumSwitch, enumBodies, enumBroken, enumValueOf) were run on JVM 25.0.5 first. The own checker decides the first four, and enumState, as the JVM does in every native mode; valueOf stays a gap. The models test covers the four that go through Enum's model. A new engine unit test covers the per-cell split merged and unmerged, and the ArrayStoreException refusal. initializer_shapes.py (static) counts 0 class-initializer gaps over the four apps, where 4b counted 49, and none over the recorded examples (013 and 071 reached four Quorum enums). Unit (154), integration (64) and skill pass. Conformance fails only its two known tests: the 12 library-record claims on JDK 25.0.5, and lib/benchmark/conformance.json, the JBMC stream's file, which is now 10 more claims behind. Three integration fixtures that used a String[] to keep an initializer out now use a double[].

The main brief's Phase 5 text says the own checker refuses arrays of references; that is no longer so, though it still refuses List.of and copyOf, whose models stay JBMC-only.

commits.summary: Put Bitwuzla behind the own checker's solver interface, chosen by JVMCONTRACT_SOLVER (Phase 6c, step 1)
commits.body: lib/src/bmc/bitwuzla.rs (new) gives Bitwuzla 0.8.2 the engine's own bit-blasted clauses through the Sat trait: each variable is a Boolean constant, each clause an 'or', each call check_sat_assuming, with the per-call limit as a termination callback. Nothing links it: the C API is loaded at run time from JVMCONTRACT_BITWUZLA or ~/tools/bitwuzla/current, and any version other than 0.8.2 is refused. JVMCONTRACT_SOLVER=bitwuzla runs every check of a process on it, and 'jvmcontract transcript --solver bitwuzla' replays a transcript on it. Results now name the solver the check ran on: solver_signature() is the configured solver's, and the outcome's short solver name comes from the solver's signature instead of a literal, so it is unchanged under CaDiCaL.

commits.summary: Make Bitwuzla's options selectable by name and queue the bit-blasted solver comparison (Phase 6c, step 2; verification pending)
commits.body:
JVMCONTRACT_SOLVER and 'jvmcontract transcript --solver' now take Bitwuzla's options after a colon, by the long names of its command line (bitwuzla:preprocess=0,rewrite-level=0). The binding (lib/src/bmc/bitwuzla.rs) reads each option's range or modes from the library through bitwuzla_get_option_info, whose C layout a test checks, and refuses a value outside them before setting it, since the C API aborts on one. It also refuses the options it sets itself (produce-models, time-limit-per, sat-solver) and string options. The solver's signature lists the options, so statements and transcript headers name the configuration. sat::named now returns a shared closure (Maker) rather than a function pointer; Options::solver is unchanged.

lib/solvers/compare.py (new, with test_compare.py) is the comparison's script. It reuses lib/benchmark/run.py's cases, compilation, command lines and measurement without changing them. It runs the five workloads where the formula's size dominates (real/midpoint/search-within-bound, example/141, example/142, held/reverse, held/prefix-sums) under strict, on cadical, bitwuzla and bitwuzla:preprocess=0, three runs each. It records the first run's transcripts, replays CaDiCaL's transcripts on all three solvers, and writes bit-blasted.json and bit-blasted.md. Queued as job 20261106-224616-the-own-checker-on-cadical-and-on-bitwuz. The brief's single 6c job becomes two: this one, SAT only, and a later one on word-level terms.

Verified inline. Unit tests (160), integration (64) and skill pass, and so do the script's 4 tests. Conformance fails only its two known tests: the 12 library-record claims, and the JBMC stream's benchmark file. held/lower-bound under bitwuzla:preprocess=0 is verified with the same transcripts, and its statement names the option. The script's trial on prefix-sums and reverse, on all three solvers, gives every verdict as expected and no replay contradiction. All five workloads on CaDiCaL give 942, 115, 18, 1,044 and 1,885 solver calls (942 and 1,044 are the review's counts).

Also recorded under Progress: the result of Phase 5's job 20261106-203501 (failed). 071 and 013 keep their violations, and the Enum and List models are no longer gaps. 071's first two proofs stay unverifiable under strict, on Collection.isEmpty/toArray stubs that jbmc_gaps.rs finds in the model's listCopy by walking JBMC's call graph; no path of these proofs reaches them. So Phase 5's criterion on 071 is not met, and the fix is in jbmc_gaps.rs, the JBMC stream's file. The JBMC conformance run also found a false success under strict: on 'declaring', JBMC 6.11.0 runs Sub.<clinit> on a getstatic of a field Holder declares, where the JVM initializes Holder alone. That is for the JBMC stream and the reconcile loop to name as a gap. The rest of the brief is accurate.

commits.summary: Give Bitwuzla the own checker's word-level terms, and queue the word-level solver comparison (Phase 6c, part 2; verification pending)
commits.body:
The solver interface (lib/src/bmc/sat.rs) gains Terms: a solver may take the formula as terms. Over such a solver the encoding (bits.rs) builds no circuits. Each gate is defined to it as a Boolean term. Each addition, subtraction, multiplication, signed division and remainder, comparison, symbolic shift, bitwise operation of two non-constant values and ite of two values is one word-level operation. Constants and a few identities still fold, and nothing is left to lazy refinement. A path's model is still evaluated by the engine, with each word-level operation computed from its operands' values. JVMCONTRACT_SOLVER=bitwuzla-words[:options] (bitwuzla.rs) makes each operation one Bitwuzla bit-vector term, with extracts for its bits, and reads runs of a term's bits back as the term. Arrays stay bounded cells read and written through ites (no array theory), and such a check refuses a transcript, since there are no clauses to record. The outcome and --json stats gain word_operations, which is left out when zero, so CaDiCaL's output is unchanged. lib/solvers/compare.py --words runs the five workloads' full checks on cadical, bitwuzla-words and bitwuzla-words:preprocess=0, and writes word-level.json and .md.

Verified inline. The blaster's int and long arithmetic tests now also run on bitwuzla-words, and the model's values match the engine's own evaluation. The Bitwuzla engine test covers the word-level solver: the same verdicts, a real violating input, and the refused transcript. The engine's unit tests with the word-level solver chosen: 46 of 51 pass. Four fail by design (they pin lazy refinement or the clauses and transcripts). One JBMC test failed once and passes alone. Unit (162), integration (64) and skill pass. Conformance fails only its two known tests: the 12 library-record claims, and the benchmark file. One inline run each, indicative only: reverse took 0.12 s on words against 0.18 s on CaDiCaL, prefix sums 0.06 s against 0.05 s, and 141 2.35 s on words. All verified.

commits.summary: Recommend against moving the own checker to word-level solving, from the two solver comparisons (Phase 6d)
commits.body:
Jobs 20261106-224616 (bit-blasted, at 09739e6) and 20261106-230455 (word-level, at bbb3062) both passed on vm-1: every check of the five workloads where the formula's size dominates (binary search, examples 141 and 142, reverse, prefix sums) is verified on every solver, with the same paths and merges, and no replay contradicts its recording. Given the engine's own clauses, Bitwuzla 0.8.2 is 2 to 43 times slower than the bundled CaDiCaL 1.9.5 with its defaults and 1.7 to 14 times with preprocess=0. Given word-level terms with preprocess=0, it is 1.93x faster on binary search, 1.66x on reverse, 1.31x on 142 and level on 141 and prefix sums; with its default preprocessing, 141 and 142 are slower than CaDiCaL.

lib/solvers/README.md (new) is Phase 6d's written case: keep CaDiCaL and bit-blasting as the default, and keep bitwuzla-words as an opt-in prototype. The solver alone gains nothing, terms gain under 2x and only with a default turned off, no case moves from undecided to decided, and a migration would cost the clause transcripts and the bundled solver while the array theory that would make it architectural is unbuilt. It says what would reopen the question (a slow check where solving dominates, such as nonlinear arithmetic or long arrays) and the evidence's limits, among them that Bitwuzla's CaDiCaL 2.1.2 against the engine's 1.9.5 isn't separated. No default changes. lib/README.md (shared) gains one sentence pointing at it.

Also fixed: both jobs' tables say 'at ?' for the commit, since the runner's exported tree has no git; compare.py now takes VERIFY_SOURCE_COMMIT first (a new test). The recorded tables stand. Verified: the script's 5 tests and the skill test pass, the page's relative links resolve, and every figure on it was recomputed from the jobs' JSON; no Rust changed. The brief's Progress records both results and sets the status to done: all of 1c, 4b, 5 and 6 are done, apart from Phase 5's last criterion (071's two proofs under strict), whose fix is in jbmc_gaps.rs, the JBMC stream's file, and is listed for the reconcile loop with the other items it inherits.

commits.summary: Merge the engines-jbmc and engines-native streams
commits.body:
Reconcile steps 1-5 of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. Both stream loops had stopped with status done. Their final session traces were recorded on their own branches first, their logs copied into this workspace, and the default line merged with jbmc@- and native@-. The generated trace files were taken from the default side and rewritten by this commit. lib/README.md's one conflict keeps both streams' text: the native stream's transcript and solver-interface paragraphs, then the JBMC stream's --confirm paragraph with its defect rule.

commits.summary: JBMC runs class initializers the JVM does not: the preflight names them as extra-initializer and refuses a JBMC proof through one (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-203501 found a false proof of JBMC under --gaps strict: conformance/declaring/2 (result == n + 107) was Verified, while the JVM returns n + 7. JBMC 6.11.0's goto listing (nothing solved) shows two shapes against JVMS 5.5: at a getstatic, putstatic or invokestatic it initializes the class the instruction names, not the class that declares the resolved member (Sub.value, declared by Holder, runs Sub.<clinit>); and initializing a class it initializes every superinterface, where the JVM initializes only those that declare a default method (conformance/defaults: 43 in JBMC, 3 on the JVM, which is why JBMC's counterexample to defaults/1 did not reproduce).

lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs compares, at each such instruction, the <clinit> calls JBMC's wrappers make with bmc::gaps::initializers of the declaring class, and names an initializer JBMC runs and the JVM does not as the defect extra-initializer, refused under every --gaps mode like the three before. The goto parser also keeps the bytecode index across JBMC's '// Labels:' comments, which had dropped it. The corpus gains defaults/3 (result == 43), the second shape's false proof (lib/benchmark/conformance.json regenerated). tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects gains the shapes in p/D.java, cause 4 in its README, and a third upstream report drafted for the user (I.java is its example, run on the JVM inline), not filed.

commits.summary: A stub JBMC's call graph reaches on no path the proof takes is no gap: the preflight reads JBMC's symbolic execution (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-203501 left example 071's first two property proofs no verdict under strict: the preflight in lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs walks JBMC's call graph, which takes every branch, and reached the stubs Collection.isEmpty and Collection.toArray in the List.copyOf model's ImmutableCollections.listCopy, which calls them only for a collection other than the immutable lists List.of makes; no path gives it one. Now, when the call graph reaches a stub, the preflight also runs JBMC's symbolic execution of the proof (jbmc --program-only with the proof's unwind, unwinding assertions and options, over every input, solving nothing). Its formula is what the proof solves, and a stub none of its steps comes from is on no path within the bounds and is no gap; the note names it ('never enters'). Steps are mapped to functions by the goto listing's location numbers, which parse_goto now records, each checked against the listing's comment for that location; a run that fails, does not finish within the preflight's minute, or does not match, leaves the call graph's gaps. Unlinked call sites, monitors and defects are still the call graph's.

Verified inline: new unit tests read locations and the symbolic execution's output (including mismatches and unfinished runs), and one runs JBMC 6.11.0 on tests/fixtures/jbmc-paths/P.java with the models: over List.of's list the two stubs are reached in the call graph and not entered, so no gap; over an opaque Collection they are entered and stay gaps. The whole Rust suite passes (unit 177, integration 64, conformance 9 with 2 ignored). lib/README.md and the module doc describe the check.

The own checker's encoding phase (lib/src/bmc/bits.rs) timed one operation in 64 at random and counted it 64 times. Nothing was built or run; the loop scripts don't know the name 'foundations' yet, which is a step after approval.

commits.summary: Revise the foundations draft after an outside review: a preservation contract inference can't weaken, and one four-stream example as the gate
commits.body:
The draft of llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md and its four stream briefs was reviewed by an outside reviewer, saved as foundations-review-draft.md (extracted from the ChatGPT share page's embedded data, unchanged apart from a header). The review kept the scope, the four-way split and the deferrals and changed the acceptance contract; the briefs now take that in. Every comparison has a preservation contract (external inputs and required observations) that inference works under and can't weaken, with observation accounting and intent kept apart from evidence; the hints file has both states. The joint example, a small kernel behind one real entry point, is the loop's gate: its fixture, golden IR files and stub interfaces are fixed in Phase 0, each stream's core includes its part of it, and a partial result is recorded as partial. run-streams.sh is to gain an integration check that merges the streams' current commits in a disposable workspace while they run, and a stream is finished only by its status, not by stopping. Heap: constructor-made domains labelled as such, identity relations compared within a version, input-object and allocation bounds apart, replay required with object inputs. Summaries: a canonical claim projection as the cache key, looked up on the prepared claim, adversarial invalidation tests, and a narrow mandatory S4 with a call-site applicability check and acyclic dependencies. Observations: effects as an ordered trace of modeled call attempts with payload snapshots, one environment model for both versions, and visible bounds. Planted defects now target the abstractions too.

One claim of the review was checked against the code rather than taken from it: shared.rs's shape is an exact fingerprint of a method body (constant-pool references and exception catch types resolved), but covers nothing outside the body, so S1 adds hierarchy, dispatch targets, annotations and configuration. Every anchor link between the briefs was checked to resolve. Still a draft: nothing was built or run.

Conflicts are reported with the files, without running the script; each check abandons the previous merge; the check stops when every stream is finished and on Ctrl-C. The engines brief names no script, so its run is unchanged. foundations' script is llm-dlc/tools/foundations-integration.sh, which runs lib/tests/foundations.rs, to be written in Phase 0. The five briefs have session ids, the streams fork from the planning session ae994066 (this one), and the main brief lists what is left before launch: rebase onto the merged engine-priorities, Phase 0 (deferred because it rewrites statement.rs, which the jbmc stream is changing), merging into the default line, closing the planning session.

commits.summary: Run the foundations loop without the verification pipeline: jobs are submitted for review after the run, never awaited
commits.body: run-streams.sh reads a new Loop setting, '- verification: separate'. For such a brief it starts no verification loop and never waits for a job: a loop whose status says 'waiting on jobs' is counted as finished, with its jobs left for review. Without the setting nothing changes, so the engines run behaves as before. foundations.md sets it. Its rule, repeated in each stream brief: heavy work is still never run inline, but is submitted with its expected verdict or figure, committed with the change, listed under Progress for review, and the loop goes on; no loop waits for, polls or reads a result, and nothing is decided from one (the conservative choice is taken and the confirming job recorded). A step is done when its code, inline tests and job submission are committed; a criterion only a job can show is met pending review. Statuses are working, done or blocked, never waiting on jobs; the reconcile folds the streams' jobs into one list for review, and waits only for uncommitted files a separately run verification loop may leave in the default working copy. The memory note in Running it all now leaves about 25 GB for such a loop. llm-dlc/README.md documents the setting.

commits.summary: Foundations: quick jobs go in at priority 10 and may be awaited briefly; long jobs are still never waited for
commits.body:
The verification rule of foundations.md and its four stream briefs now tells jobs apart by their estimate. A quick job, a few minutes or less, is submitted with --priority 10 so a runner takes it before the long ones, and the session may await it inside its cycle: work on, poll pipeline.py status about once a minute, for at most 15 minutes after submitting, and use the result like an inline one if it is back. Otherwise, and for every long job, the job is listed for review after the run and not polled or read again. Waiting never ends a cycle or sets a status, so run-streams.sh, which waits for no job under '- verification: separate', is unchanged apart from its header comment; the bound keeps a run from hanging when no verification loop is running. The done criteria and llm-dlc/README.md say the same.

Checked that pipeline.py submit takes --priority (higher runs first; the pipeline README's example uses 10) and that status lists every workspace's jobs; bash -n on run-streams.sh. Documentation and brief changes only.

commits.summary: A brief template with standing rules, the timebox first: an item that fails verification twice in a row is deferred with its finding
commits.body:
Steering a running loop from outside takes a brief edit, and a brief edit stops the loop at the next cycle, so rules a run may need belong in the brief before it starts. llm-dlc/loops/brief-template.md (new) gives the skeleton of a brief, its Loop settings keys, the two verification modes, and the standing rules every brief starts with. The first is the timebox: an item whose verification fails twice in a row (two jobs, or two inline attempts; a failure, a timeout or an out-of-memory; a resubmission with a larger budget counts) is logged under Progress as deferred by the timebox, with both attempts, the finding, and what a further attempt would try and cost, and the loop moves on. There is no third attempt: an item that fails twice has very likely been underestimated, its proof needing far more depth than the plan allowed, and it is handled separately in another session after careful consideration by a person. A rule like it would have stopped the engine-priorities loop's retries on example 071 a day earlier.

The foundations brief and its four streams take the rule: under separate verification it counts the failures a loop sees (quick jobs that came back, inline attempts); a stream whose core item is deferred ends blocked naming it; a joint-example row whose item is deferred makes Phase 5 partial; the reconcile lists every deferred item first for review; and no Loop until treats a deferral as a reason to go on. llm-dlc/README.md lists the template. Every anchor link between the briefs resolves, apart from one inside the template's fenced skeleton, which belongs to the brief made from it.

commits.summary: run-streams.sh: a status bar of every loop's cycle, commits, spend and state, and tmux scrollback that works over ssh
commits.body: Started inside tmux, run-streams.sh turns the mouse on for the session so the wheel scrolls back through the output (Ctrl-b [ also works). A pane keeps the history limit it was made with, and tmux's default is 2000 lines, so when the pane keeps fewer than RUN_STREAMS_HISTORY (200000) the script raises the session's limit and goes on in a new window, streams-NAME, passing on the RUN_STREAMS_, FEATURE_LOOP_ and VERIFICATION_LOOP_ settings; the window stays open with the output after the run until Enter (RUN_STREAMS_NEW_WINDOW=no stays in the pane). A status bar at the bottom of the pane (pane-border-status, refreshed every RUN_STREAMS_STATUS_EVERY seconds, 15) shows the run's age and total spend, the integration check's last result, and per loop its current cycle, its commits, its spend, its brief's status or how it finished, and how long since its last output line; the same line is logged every half hour, or every quarter hour outside tmux. Each loop's output now goes through llm-dlc/tools/streams_status.py tag, which prefixes it as sed did and records the 'turn done' dollar figures, the cycle and the last activity in llm-dlc/loop-summaries/run-streams-NAME/; spend and the run's start survive a restart. Commits are counted from the loops' run records.

commits.summary: The foundations run stays in its tmux pane: '- new-window: no', a brief setting RUN_STREAMS_NEW_WINDOW overrides; and closing the pane no longer leaves loops running
commits.body:
run-streams.sh reads '- new-window: yes|no' from the brief's Loop settings, RUN_STREAMS_NEW_WINDOW winning over it, so moving to a new window with a long history stays available for later briefs. foundations.md sets no: its run stays in the pane it was started in, with the bar there; since that pane keeps the history it was made with, the script raises the session's limit for new panes and says so, and the brief says to start in a pane made after 'tmux set -g history-limit 200000'. A value other than yes or no exits with status 2. The template lists the key.

Testing it showed a bug from the previous commit: the status bar's loop runs in a process group of its own, so killing the tmux server left it running, and it went on writing to a later server of the same name. run-streams.sh now treats a hangup like Ctrl-C (stop every loop), and the status bar and the integration check end when the script is gone. Verified in an isolated tmux server (tmux -L) with stub loops: the brief's no kept the run in window 0 with the bar and raised the session's history-limit; RUN_STREAMS_NEW_WINDOW=yes moved it to streams-foundations; 'maybe' exited 2; and killing the server three seconds into a run left no process behind. The two renderers orphaned by the earlier tests were stopped.

commits.summary: Recheck the foundations brief against main after the engine-priorities merge
commits.body:
The brief's starting point was recounted at e42ea83, before the engines merge. Rechecked on main at ea315037: line numbers moved (Val::R at bmc/mod.rs:316, same_shape :486, unsupported_parameter :290, record_of equivalence.rs:616, the refusals that suggest an expression :768-810); arrays of references (anewarray, aaload, aastore over known objects or null) and application static fields with class initialization are now implemented, so the heap stream's H0 is marked done; and aliasing among objects a method makes itself is already decided (aliasedLocals, aliasedObjects, writeThrough have verdicts), so H1 keeps those verdicts rather than earning them, and H2's first targets are the conformance cases outside the domain for their inputs: twoArrays with the same array twice, and length and lengthOrMinusOne with a null array. Parameters are still primitives and primitive arrays only.

Checked by reading the merged code and lib/tests/conformance.rs; a brief change only.

commits.summary: Foundations Phase 0: the shared IR in lib/src/spec, each stream's interface, and the joint example as an executable integration contract
commits.body:
lib/src/spec/mod.rs holds the types the four foundations streams meet at, serializable both ways: a comparison's preservation contract (external inputs and the observations the old version is held to), the object domain (classes, input-object and allocation bounds per version, nullability, aliasing, how inputs are made and the label a result states), observations beyond result and exception (field paths, identity relations within a version, effects as modeled call attempts, status), the environment model (one for both versions, exact order, a trace bound), the correspondence between old and new internal states, of which --before-arguments and --results-agree-when are special cases (Correspondence::from_flags), the hints file with intent and evidence kept apart, the canonical claim with nothing result-dependent in it, and an outcome with its observation accounting. Statement gains an optional spec field, None everywhere, so no recorded result changes. heap.rs (check), cache.rs (key, lookup, store, callee_reuse), observe.rs (entry_points, compare, effect_log, check) and align.rs (propose) are the streams' interfaces, each returning a named Unsupported until its stream does its part.

lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/ is the joint example: a pricing kernel behind one real annotated route (POST /quotes, which sends a QuoteEvent), refactored from a primitive amount to a Money value object with a rewritten discount helper, six defects overlaid on the refactor (offset, alias-to-copy, dropped-effect, duplicated-effect, outside-domain, route-change), a string route left unresolved, and golden files of its IR with the verdict every case must reach. All eight builds compile against the Spring stand-ins, and on a real JVM (JDK 25.0.5) before and after agree on every probed input while each defect differs exactly where intended (outside-domain not at all through the constructor). lib/tests/foundations.rs checks that the golden files round-trip through the types and runs 24 checks over the four parts: all unsupported now, none failing; foundations-integration.sh passes on it. The briefs record Phase 0, the interface each stream owns, the reserved example numbers (150-199) and a pre-existing flaky timing test in bmc/bits.rs that failed once in three unit runs under load; lib/README.md describes the IR.

Verified inline: cargo build; the spec unit tests (3); tests/foundations.rs (3 tests, 24 checks unsupported, 0 failed); the unit suite (183 passing in two of three runs, the flaky timing test failing in the third); tests/integration.rs (64 passed). No job submitted: nothing here is a proof.
